sections.html: The type locality is given as: Creek at left bank of Rio Cururu, tributary of upper River Tapajós near Maloca do Conzale, about 7°45’S, 58°00’W, Pará State, Brazil. According to the exporter, the species comes from the Rio Jamanxim, a tributary of the Tapajós.

Two long-snouted species from the Rio Tapajós catchment, described in 1972 and 1976, remained a mystery: Brochis bifasciata and B. ornata (both originally described as Corydoras species). Specimens of Brochis ornata corresponding exactly to the original description have still not been imported, whereas B. bifasciata has finally been imported recently. Why this long-snouted fish is so rare is unknown.

Brochis bifasciata is the long-snouted version of the very beautiful Hoplisoma sp. CW127, which is also very difficult to obtain. Hoplisoma sp. C133 is very similar to CW127 and lacks the black zone in the dorsal fin that merges into a shoulder band running towards the belly; it was also occasionally imported with the origin "Tapajós". This pattern is typical for Hoplisoma sp. CW127 and is also found in B. bifasciata. For Hoplisoma sp. C133 there is an identically marked long-snouted Brochis species, which as far as is known has not yet been assigned a C or CW number.

There is another number, Brochis sp. CW135, for a fish very similar to B. bifasciata that is imported together with it. These animals have a slightly different dorsal pattern. This is considered to fall within the variance of B. bifasciata, and since the CW135 phenotype has so far appeared only in single specimens, it is not offered separately.

In the type specimen of B. bifasciata, the lower of the two longitudinal bands runs along the midline, where the two rows of lateral bone plates meet. In the current import, there are also specimens in which the second longitudinal band runs clearly below the midline. Overall, B. bifasciata appears to be as variable as B. pulcher.
